Assertions.Description: With Open as administrator off and a medium-integrity Runner, the actual Settings launch opens a usable non-elevated editor; an owned synthetic save shows the non-admin error and leaves hosts bytes unchanged.

With Open as administrator on, no borrowed editor and authorized secure-desktop consent where required, actual Settings launch creates an elevated editor that can save the synthetic entry. Event delivery or direct elevated launch is not this observation.
After enabling the startup warning through Settings, the warning appears and Quit closes the owned editor/process.
On a fresh launch with the warning enabled, Accept dismisses the warning while leaving a usable editor open.
After turning the warning off through Settings, a fresh launch is usable without that warning; the original preference is restored.
Disabling only Hosts through Settings persists the disabled state, disables its launch action and does not activate an editor.
Re-enabling Hosts through Settings persists the enabled state and its real launch action opens a usable editor.
When all affected borrowed state can be preserved across an authorized full PowerToys restart, the disabled Hosts setting and inactive behavior survive that restart.
When all affected borrowed state can be preserved across an authorized full PowerToys restart, the enabled Hosts setting and usable launch survive that restart.
Opening the real tray Quick Access surface and invoking its enabled Hosts launcher entry opens the intended editor.
Disabling Hosts through Quick Access removes its launcher entry and updates the already-open Hosts Settings page to disabled.
Re-enabling Hosts through Quick Access restores its launcher entry and updates the already-open Hosts Settings page to enabled; original flyout state is preserved.
Creating a collision-checked tagged entry through the product dialog produces the correct address, hosts, comment and active state in its row without removing unrelated entries.
With an authorized elevated writer, the committed synthetic entry is independently observed in the actual hosts file with the requested mapping; unrelated mappings remain intact.
A safely owned real auto-refreshing text editor already open on the actual hosts file displays that synthetic committed mapping without manual reload. A private file read is insufficient.
A new-entry draft with a valid loopback address and exactly nine unique reserved-domain hostnames enables Add.
Changing that draft to ten hostnames disables Add; Cancel leaves the hosts file unchanged.
With an elevated writer, toggling the owned row off shows it inactive and comments its mapping in the file without changing unrelated mappings.
Toggling the owned row on shows it active and uncomments its mapping in the file without changing unrelated mappings.
After a guarded append of one tagged ten-host line and the product's external-change Reload, the UI contains exactly the nine-host and one-host split rows with every synthetic hostname retained.
Loading that overlong line shows the too-many-hosts teaching tip/info message. Restoring the file is followed by separate live-cache reload verification.
The address filter finds the intended owned row among distinguishable prepared entries, without claiming preparation as product filtering.
The hostname filter finds the intended owned row among distinguishable prepared entries.
The comment filter finds the intended owned row among distinguishable prepared entries.
A collision-checked nonmatching filter query yields the product's no-matching-entries state.
Clear filters returns the original visible entry set, retaining all unrelated entries.

The actual Open hosts file control opens the actual hosts document in Windows Notepad on builds containing #46194; older builds use the configured default editor. The resulting document/tab and pre-existing editor sessions are preserved.

Selecting Top through Settings persists the choice, and committing preserved original additional content plus a tagged comment through the editor places that comment before the synthetic mapping in the file.
Selecting Bottom through Settings persists the choice, and an actual editor commit places the tagged comment after the synthetic mapping; original content and preference are restored.
After selecting a fresh owned backup folder through Settings and enabling backup, the first edit in a fresh elevated editor creates a backup there containing the exact pre-edit hosts bytes.
A second edit in the same editor process creates no second backup.
With backup disabled through Settings, the first edit in a fresh elevated editor creates no backup; original backup preferences and files are preserved.
With an isolated selected folder containing only owned synthetic backup fixtures and a sentinel, Never selected through Settings retains every fixture after elevated editor startup.
Count-based retention selected through Settings retains exactly the configured newest count of owned backups and leaves the non-backup sentinel unchanged after elevated startup.

Age-and-count retention selected through Settings removes only expired owned backups beyond the protected newest count; recent backups, protected newest backups and the non-backup sentinel survive elevated startup.
An ordinary editor starts with a nonempty appropriate title and remains usable without a title-bar startup crash.
An elevated editor starts with the appropriate nonempty administrator title and remains usable without a title-bar startup crash.
In an affected installed CJK Windows display language with PowerToys language set to Windows Default, ordinary editor startup remains usable with a nonempty appropriate title.

In an affected installed CJK Windows display language with PowerToys language set to Windows Default and authorized elevation, elevated editor startup remains usable with a nonempty appropriate title.

On supported Windows, selecting Light default app mode through Windows Settings while the editor is live produces visible, legible caption-button glyphs; a reopen or PowerToys-only theme change is not equivalent.
Selecting Dark Windows default app mode while the same editor is live produces visible, legible caption-button glyphs, followed by verified original app-mode and Windows Settings restoration.
With an installed authorized non-English Windows display language, Hosts command labels, warning, tooltips and dialogs follow that language; English-only observations do not satisfy this condition.
With an authorized supported non-English language and the localized PowerToys extension, Hosts ordinary/admin launch titles and subtitles and the Settings subtitle show the expected translations.
Invoking ordinary Hosts launch in the actual PowerToys Command Palette extension opens the intended ordinary editor, not an app-search shortcut or a directly signaled event.
Invoking the extension's administrator launch with authorized consent creates the intended elevated editor; event delivery alone is insufficient.
The extension's Hosts Settings command lands on the actual Hosts Settings page.
When Hosts is disabled, both extension launch commands are unavailable while the Hosts Settings command remains available.

On a build containing #50935, pressing Ctrl+Shift+Enter on the selected ordinary Hosts launch command invokes its administrator action and reaches an elevated editor with authorized consent; menu invocation is a separate path.
Pinning the ordinary Hosts launch command survives reopening Command Palette and that pin still launches the intended editor; original pin state/order is restored.
Pinning the administrator Hosts launch command survives reopening and remains independently usable with authorized elevation consent; original pin state/order is restored.
Pinning Hosts Settings survives reopening and remains independently usable at the correct page; original pin state/order is restored.

Changing only ordinary Hosts launch's fallback setting persists across reopening extension settings without changing administrator launch or Hosts Settings fallback preferences; original preferences are restored.

An authorized clean-install fixture containing #47144 leaves Hosts disabled from first Runner startup through first Settings persistence without transient activation; existing settings must not be deleted to simulate this fixture.
Actual Check for updates, without installing, leaves the explicit Hosts enabled preference unchanged before cleanup.
With authorized diagnostic/backup-status fixtures, read-only status refreshes leave Hosts enablement unchanged rather than submitting cached general settings.
In an isolated authorized lifecycle fixture, an early Settings request observes fully initialized Hosts enablement rather than persisting a partial startup state.

In an isolated authorized module-load-failure fixture, Hosts' explicit enabled setting survives the missing runtime module and is available when it loads again; installed binaries are not renamed in the shared run.

In an isolated authorized originally-missing-enabled-key fixture, changing Hosts enablement through real Settings persists the requested state; existing general settings are not damaged to manufacture absence.
In an authorized Windows shutdown/restart fixture, the Hosts preference and valid general settings survive without the exit-time wipe; do not reboot the shared desktop.

With Diagnostic data and Enable viewing authorized and enabled before the required PowerToys restart, the actual Diagnostic data viewer contains Hosts event XML corresponding to the recorded actions; consent/viewing state is restored and unrelated payloads stay private.
